interfaces.name: Web application
interfaces.classification_rationale: Actions are expressed by manipulating presented affordances (registration, chat, Q&A, polls, CTA, screen share, Go Live) of a persistent navigable representation of the event; primitive is affordance manipulation with consumer-driven control.

provenance.evidence: Official guide describing the browser-based hosting UI and its interactive engagement controls.
Current (Aug 2026) provider doc confirming browser-based access for hosts and attendees.

interfaces.name: Mobile app
interfaces.classification_rationale: First-party native client where the consumer manipulates on-screen affordances (chat, polls, upvote questions) of the event representation; same paradigm as web on a distinct client surface and runtime.

provenance.evidence: Provider (Crowdcast Inc.) App Store listing for the first-party mobile client.
Current provider doc stating attendees can use the Crowdcast app for Android or iOS.

interfaces.name: RTMP ingest (RTMP Mode)
interfaces.technology: RTMP/RTMPS publish to Server URL + Stream Key
interfaces.classification_rationale: The consumer explicitly invokes a provider-defined publish operation, pushing a stream from an external encoder to a provider ingest endpoint identified by Server URL and Stream Key, analogous to SMTP submission or Git remote push.

provenance.evidence: Current (Jun 2026) official RTMP Mode doc defining the ingest endpoint and stream key publishing flow from OBS, Wirecast, Ecamm, vMix.

access_mechanism_ledger.detail: No native desktop app found; hosting and attending are done via browser.
No command-line interface or TUI dashboard documented.

Third-party integration platform; underlying API is partner-scoped and documented only for Zapier, with no public operation/base/auth reference to reconstruct a directly consumable Programmatic interface.

access_mechanism_ledger.mechanism: Native API / event webhooks (registration, question, session-ended triggers)
access_mechanism_ledger.detail: Surfaced only through Zapier; provider sources do not establish native push webhooks versus Zapier polling, so no Event interface is established. No evidence is not absence.
Third-party integrations for payments and membership access; not a mechanism for accessing the service.
Embedded instance of the web application; same interaction contract, not a distinct interface.
Outbound restream feature from Crowdcast to third parties; not a way to access Crowdcast.
